value.text: I need to count call sites per unique function name, so I'm writing a bash loop that greps for name patterns across all Go files repo-wide, excluding declaration lines.

args.command: cd /bench/repo && grep -rhoE '^func (\([^)]*\) )?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\(' internal --include='*.go' | sed -E 's/^func (\([^)]*\) )?//; s/\($//' | sort -u > /tmp/names.txt && wc -l /tmp/names.txt && : > /tmp/counts.txt && while read -r n; do c=$(grep -rhoE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.])${n}\(" --include='*.go' . | wc -l); cm=$(grep -rhoE "\.${n}\(" --include='*.go' . | wc -l); d=$(grep -rhcE "^func (\([^)]*\) )?${n}\(" -r --include='*.go' . | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END{print s}'); echo "$n plain=$c meth=$cm decl=$d"; done < /tmp/names.txt > /tmp/counts.txt; sort -t= -k2 -rn /tmp/counts.txt | head -5

value.text:
I've confirmed CompileToStatement has the most call sites overall at 37-38, though most are tests with only 7 production callers, while addArg leads when counting production code only.

Since CompileToStatement wins on both total call sites and distinct callers (36 vs addArg's 14), I'll lead with that as the primary answer, while noting the caveat that this analysis is text-based without an actual Go toolchain.

h10.

`(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go:74` — approx 37 call sites (~36 distinct calling functions)

That is the highest by raw inbound-call count anywhere in the repo, but the makeup matters: 30 of those calls come from tests in `internal/filter/engine_test.go`, `internal/filter/functions_test.go`, and `internal/filter/time_test.go` (each test function calls it about once). Only 7 calls are from production code — `filter.AppendConditions` in `internal/filter/helpers.go`, `validateAttachmentFilter` in `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go`, `validateFilter` in `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go`, and `ListMemoRelations` in each of `store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go`, `store/db/postgres/memo_relation.go` (2 calls), and `store/db/mysql/memo_relation.go`.

If you exclude tests, the leader changes: `(*renderer).addArg` in `internal/filter/render.go:842` has 28 call sites, all in non-test code, spread across 14 distinct renderer methods in the same file (`renderTagInList` alone calls it 6 times, `renderElementInCondition` and `foldedLike` 3 each). Runner-up overall is `util.GenUUID` in `internal/util/util.go:40` with 28 call sites, though 21 of those are in test files, leaving 7 production callers in `server/auth/token.go` and the `server/router/api/v1` services.

One caveat on method: the Go toolchain isn't installed in this environment, so these are textual call-site counts rather than a type-resolved call graph. I filtered out same-named symbols from other packages (for example `Error`, `New`, and `Len` have hundreds of repo-wide matches that belong to the standard library and generated protobuf code, not to `internal/`), and I verified each candidate's declaration site, but counts could be off by a small amount where a name is shadowed.
